hops.title: Say it: a hummingbird packs its own fuel
hops.text: Try saying, "A hummingbird does not pack a suitcase. It packs its own fuel tank." Use it when your child wonders how such a tiny bird makes such a long trip. A ruby-throated hummingbird can nearly double its weight, from about 3.25 to 6 grams, before a nonstop flight of about 500 miles across the Gulf of Mexico.

sources.citation: USDA Forest Service, Pollinator of the Month: Ruby-throated Hummingbird.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A ruby-throated hummingbird flying over blue ocean waves under a clear autumn sky.
image.caption: A ruby-throated hummingbird can nearly double its weight before crossing about 500 miles of open water.

hops.title: Point at it: a puffed-up bird on a cold day
hops.text: During your window watch, or outside with you right beside your child, look for a bird sitting round and puffy on a branch. Fluffed feathers trap warm air next to its skin, like a down vest. Resting birds often tuck their bare feet into their belly feathers on cold days. Can you spot one with hidden feet?

sources.citation: Purdue University College of Agriculture, "How do birds that stay north survive Indiana's winter?", February 2022.

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A small bird puffed up round on a snowy branch with its feet hidden in its feathers.
image.caption: Fluffed feathers trap a layer of warm air close to a winter bird's skin.

hops.title: Compare it: a deer coat is like a raincoat over a fleece
hops.text: Next time you zip a raincoat over a fleece sweater, tell your child white-tailed deer wear the same two-layer outfit. Long, hollow outer hairs help keep water out, while the thick, soft fur underneath holds warm air close to the skin. It keeps heat in so well that snow can sit on a deer's back without melting.

sources.citation: Penn State Deer-Forest Study, "Guaranteed to Last" (Jeannine Fleegle).
Penn State Department of Animal Science, "Deer in Winter."

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A white-tailed deer in a thick winter coat standing in snowy woods with snow on its back.
image.caption: A deer's two-layer winter coat keeps heat in so well that snow rests on its back unmelted.
